company.name: Stanford Institute for Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence

profile_text.body:
The Stanford Institute for Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence, also known as Stanford HAI, HAI, and AI Index, is a nonprofit university lab founded in 2019 and headquartered in Stanford, CA, USA. The institute describes its mission as advancing humanity through AI and data science, with work focused on discovery, technological innovation, educational transformation, and societal impact. It states that the combined institute retains the Stanford HAI name and is led by computer scientist James Landay. Co-founder Fei-Fei Li serves as Special Advisor on AI and joins John Hennessy as co-chair of the institute's advisory council.

No commercial AI products or MCP servers are listed for the institute. Its activities include research grant programs, fellowships, training for policymakers, business leaders, and K-12 educators, policy work, and student affinity groups. The site describes a human-centered AI approach that prioritizes human needs, values, and well-being, and it features research and commentary on topics such as open-source models, AI privacy, AI in healthcare, AI-generated CSAM, and language digitization.

The institute has no listed lawsuits and is associated with 281 California legal exposure entries.
